name: Music-Synchronized Animation
visualIdentity: Explicit: a timing method applicable to different aesthetics, in the Motion Design and Cinematography category, not a fixed look. Reveals, cuts, and accents are placed on identified beats, downbeats, and musical sections. Visual density follows musical energy, using anticipation and pauses.
suitableUses: Explicit: applicable to various aesthetics; source combinations name music videos and lyric videos. Inferred: rhythm-led music videos where picture must track sound. Explainer or product uses are unspecified.
limitations: Explicit: elements must not all start on one beat, and reading time must not be eliminated. The style supplies no visuals, genre, tempo, or palette, so a supporting visual style is required. Detected beats need manual verification.
palette: Not defined by the style. A reference-dependent example applies only when no approved palette is supplied: background #F3EBDD, foreground #293B44, accent_1 #628C98, accent_2 #BA7B61. Gradients are disabled. Foreground on background is 9.836:1; accents fail the 4.5:1 text target, so they are decorative only. Supplied colors override these.
motionAndInteraction: Explicit: motion syncs to measured beats and sections, with reading holds. Coherent easing is optional, and deliberate cuts and impacts stay sharp. Video runs on seekable composition time; scroll or pointer input applies only to interactive delivery. Optional mo.js bursts on beats do not detect beats themselves.
audio: Central to the method: audio analysis drives picture and sound from one shared event table. Genre, tempo, voiceover, and sound effects are unspecified. Inferred: clear-beat background music fits, and speech must stay intelligible if narration is added. No audio asset is supplied; use task-provided or authorized audio.
assetRequirements: Requires a task-provided or authorized audio file. librosa detects beats, onsets, and energy, saved as JSON timestamps; NumPy handles geometry and arrays. Fonts and assets must load before rendering. Subject, copy, and scene assets are unspecified; listed scene and aspect-ratio values are optional examples.
combinations: Source-suggested: style-094 (abstract shapes dividing on beats, primary palette only) for music videos, and style-093 (lyric words landing on stressed beats with reading holds) for lyric videos. Motion references motion-012, motion-014, and motion-015 are optional and require scene compatibility.
productionApproach: Analyze audio, verify beats manually, and save one shared event table for picture and sound. HyperFrames is the primary pipeline: a paused GSAP timeline registered in window.__timelines, checked and snapshotted before rendering. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or blocked by a verified limitation, with the reason recorded. The style renderer and motion engine own visuals and movement; the pipeline only assembles and exports.
